properties.statement:
MEASURED 2026-08-18, and the question is Anthony's: not why REFLOW2's own graph lacks this vocabulary, but WHETHER AN ARBITRARY PROJECT USING REFLOW2 WOULD EVER GET IT. 'we are just applying reflow2 back on itself here, but that is not the main concern. it is that reflow2 does SE for the projects that it is used on.'

FOR VOCABULARY TO APPEAR IN A USER'S DESIGN, THREE LEGS MUST ALL BE PRESENT:
  (1) a TYPED TOOL that writes it — raw create_node/create_edge does not count, since an agent must first know the field exists;
  (2) an INSTRUCTION, in a served skill or a tool description, saying WHEN to write it;
  (3) a DETECTOR that notices its ABSENCE, so the loop asks rather than waiting to be told.
Missing any one leaves the vocabulary empty in EVERY project, not just this one. The three cases measured here each fail differently, which is why they are worth separating:

  Capability.inputs / outputs / capability_type
    typed tool   NO  — add_capability takes id, name, description, status. Nothing else.
    instruction  NO  — 0 of 20 served skills mention inputs or outputs.
    detector     NO  — detect.rs contains no reference to either.
    => ALL THREE LEGS MISSING. No user project can acquire a capability's functional signature by any route reflow2 offers. This is the vocabulary for what a black box IS, and `req:recursive-black-box-decomposition` (accepted the same day) is the intent it serves.

  SPECIFIES
    typed tool   NO  — there is no `specifies` tool; the toolsnaps hold `documents` and nothing else in that family.
    instruction  YES — link-artifacts says, of a machine-readable contract: 'that is SPECIFIES, on the interface it defines.'
    detector     NO.
    => THE SKILL INSTRUCTS AN AGENT TO DRAW AN EDGE NO TOOL DRAWS. The only route is hand-rolled create_edge, which is the escape hatch the reachability requirement says must not count as reachability.

  DECOMPOSES
    typed tool   YES — `decomposes(from_id, to_id)`.
    instruction  YES — two skills discuss decomposition.
    detector     PARTIAL, and this is the subtle one.
    => `DecompositionCoverage` fires on a Requirement CARRYING AN INCOMING DECOMPOSES EDGE. It checks whether an existing decomposition is covered; it cannot ask why none exists. So a project that never decomposes anything gets ZERO decomposition findings and reads as coherent. All three legs look present and the vocabulary still stays empty — which is how reflow2's own graph reached 0 DECOMPOSES edges while shipping the detector for them.

⭐ THE GENERAL FINDING, and it is about the PRODUCT rather than the self-host: reflow2's detectors largely check the CONSISTENCY OF WHAT EXISTS. Some do check absence — `unsatisfied_requirement`, `unallocated_capability` — but those are absences of REQUIRED structure. Nothing asks 'you have never used this vocabulary at all', so optional vocabulary is invisible to the loop that exists to surface gaps, in every project, forever. `rule:the-self-host-always-trails-what-it-teaches` is the right frame: this is now catchable for everyone.
